section_1.title: The Setup: A Curious Mechanical System
section_1.content: Introduce the physical system: two blocks of different masses on a frictionless surface, with a wall to the left. The smaller block is placed between the wall and the larger block. All collisions are perfectly elastic.
section_1.example: A small toy mouse (mass 1kg) sits between a wall and a heavy elephant (mass 100kg). As the elephant slides toward the mouse, they begin a series of high-speed 'ping-pong' collisions.

section_2.title: Prerequisite Knowledge: Conservation Laws
section_2.content: Briefly explain that in elastic collisions, both momentum and kinetic energy are conserved. Visualize this using vector arrows (momentum) and energy bars to show how the blocks trade velocities.
section_2.example: Show a visual animation where the 'speed bars' change length exactly according to the mass ratios when they hit, ensuring total energy remains constant.

section_3.title: The Mathematical Mapping: Collision Count as Digits
section_3.content: Reveal the core discovery: If the mass of the large block is 100^n kg, the total number of collisions between the blocks and the wall will yield the first (n+1) digits of Pi.
section_3.example: Show a counter on screen: When mass ratio is 1:1, total collisions = 3. When 1:100, collisions = 31. When 1:10,000, collisions = 314.

section_4.title: Visualizing the 'Phase Space' Geometry
section_4.content: Explain that the collisions aren't magic; they are geometry. By mapping the velocities as coordinates on a 2D plane, the path of the blocks traces a circular arc that hits a 'barrier' at specific intervals.
section_4.example: A graphical representation of a bouncing ball in a circular 'wedge' sector, where the angle of the wedge is determined by the ratio of the square roots of the masses.

section_5.title: Conclusion: Why Pi Appears Everywhere
section_5.content: Summarize that Pi is a fundamental constant of rotation and circles, which inherently appear whenever we calculate repeated oscillations or collisions in constrained space.
section_5.example: A final fast-paced animation showing a 1:1,000,000 ratio block system rapidly clicking 3,141 times, concluding with the image of a circle appearing from the data.

        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)

        lecture_texts = [Text(f"- {line}", font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]

        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 1.0 + j * 1.2
                y = 2.5 - i * 1.0
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]

        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
